Two DIFFERENT relationships to `serP`, both confirmed by line-level read: (1) `buildSceneJson` calls `serP` INTERNALLY (engine-bridge.js:1605, `var sd = fastRef ? null : serP(sub);`) on an exploded CompoundPath sub-path when the retained-path optimization (CLAUDE.md §5ter) cannot apply, and `onionLayerItems` (called by `buildOnionSkinItems`/`buildGhostAllItems`) calls it again at engine-bridge.js:2731 but reads ONLY `sd.segments` from the result, sourcing every other field (fillColor/strokeColor/strokeWidth/strokeCap/strokeJoin) directly from the parent CompoundPath instead. (2) Independently of those two calls, `buildSceneJson` reads persisted-field NAMES directly off live Paper.js items' `.data` (not off a `serP`-produced dict) for its main per-layer render loop. Field-presence grep (`grep -c '\bFIELD\b' src/js/engine-bridge.js`) across every field this scope's packets emit shows the render path does NOT read, by name, anywhere in the file: `hasRealStroke`, `isFillShape`, `isFillCloseLine`, `strokeProfile`, `profileBase`, `fillSeed`, `fillSeeds`, `fillGapPx`, `fillWalls`, `tweenOn`, `xformAnchorKey`, `brushTexturePreset`, `bitmapPressureProfile`, `preTextureOpacity`, `preTextureStroke`, `shadowSwatchId`, `ownerName`, `revisionAction`, `preRevisionOpacity`, `trackRoleId`, `attachedToRoleId`, `attachOffset`, `elemHidden`, `isVectorText`, `vectorChar`, `charIndex`, `wordIndex`, `lineIndex`, `isText`, `vectorFont`, `textSize`, `textColor`, `textAlign`, `textFixedWidth`, `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `strike`, `letterSpacing`, `wordSpacing`, `lineHeightMult`, `textCase` (41 fields, zero grep hits each) — these exist purely for editor bookkeeping (fill-regen tracking, brush-texture regenerate, team-review UI, tracked-role attach, vector-text re-edit popover/Text-Animator grouping, Typography-panel checkboxes), never consumed by the render path, which draws each item from its already-baked `segments`/colors regardless. Every OTHER field this scope emits (`segments`, `closed`, `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeCap`, `strokeJoin`, `miterLimit`, `fillColor`, `opacity`, `dashArray`, `dashOffset`, `paintOrder`, `isVectorBrush`, `centerSegments`, `widthProfile`, `strokeId`, `brushGroupId`, `isLinkedFillCompanion`, `linkedFillId`, `xformAnchorCustom` [via `state.xformAnchorCustom`, not a per-item read, see `C21c.serp-core-return-fields`'s own effects], `isBrushTextureCopy`, `bitmapBrushSpec`, `channelTag`, `ownerId`, `ownerColor`, `revisionParentId`, `isRevisionGhost`, `fillGradient`, `groupId`, `paramShape`, `effects`, `isTextRoot`, `text`, `anchorTopLeft`, `isMask`, `maskMode`, `maskFeather`, `strokeGradientAlongPath`, `boxAngle`) has at least one non-comment grep hit in engine-bridge.js — this is a coarse presence check (name-in-file), not a proof every hit is a genuine per-item field read; two spot-checks (`xformAnchorCustom`, `text`) confirmed at least one hit each is a different kind of reference (a `state.*` field or an unrelated identifier substring), so this disposition should be read as 'named in the file', not 'definitely consumed per-item' for every field with a non-zero count.

future_proposals: Two textually different fallback literals (`serP`'s `'#ffffff'` at line 715 vs. `desP`'s `'#fff'` at app.js:853) exist for what the comments describe as the same semantic case (a falsy, non-exempted `strokeColor`) — functionally equivalent as CSS/hex colors, but a future consumer that does a literal STRING comparison against one or the other (rather than parsing the color) would behave inconsistently depending on whether it reads a freshly-`serP`'d dict or one that has round-tripped through `desP` at least once; not flagged as a bug (no such literal-string comparison was found in this census's own grep passes), only as a latent inconsistency worth a future consumer's awareness.

Eleven vector-text/typography fields (`isVectorText` through `textCase`, packets `serp-paramshape-text-fields`/`serp-typography-mask-gradient-fields`) and `hasRealStroke`/`ownerName`/`revisionAction`/`preRevisionOpacity`/`shadowSwatchId`/`fillSeed`-family/`tweenOn`/`xformAnchorKey`/`brushTexturePreset`/`bitmapPressureProfile`/`preTextureOpacity`/`preTextureStroke`/`trackRoleId`/`attachedToRoleId`/`attachOffset`/`elemHidden` are confirmed (by name-absence grep) to be pure editor-bookkeeping fields the render path never reads by name — a future modularity pass could consider whether these belong in a SEPARATE editor-metadata sidecar object rather than inline in the same dict `buildSceneJson`/export.js/tweens.js all read from, though CLAUDE.md §1's own 'family of bug #1' warning (a new tag missed by one of several independent consumers) argues for keeping a SINGLE flat dict rather than splitting it, so this is flagged as a discussion point, not a recommendation.

The `lineHeightMult`/`textCase` default-elision pattern (omit if equal to the hardcoded default `1.25`/`'none'`) is NOT used by any other field in this scope (every other omission rule is falsy/`undefined`-based, never 'equals a specific non-falsy default') — a future reader adding a new Typography field by copy-pasting an adjacent line could easily miss this asymmetry and under- or over-persist a value; not a current bug, just a footgun shape worth naming.

`onionLayerItems`'s own use of `serP(sub)` (engine-bridge.js:2731) to extract only `.segments`/`.closed` while discarding 96%+ of the returned dict's fields is a working but arguably wasteful pattern (constructing ~76 conditional field computations to use two of them) — flagged as a possible future micro-optimization (a narrower `segmentsOf(sub)` helper), not verified by profiling in this census.
